rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient spanning the full usable organic range at mid temperature to reveal the retention spread of all 10 compounds and whether any fail to elute by 42 min. A 20 min gradient gives useful separation information without being excessively steep or slow for the first screen.

All 10 compounds eluted with excellent resolution and the score is limited only by run time, so the next step is to steepen the gradient to shorten retention while checking whether the closest cluster around rows 5–7 remains adequately resolved. Keeping composition range and temperature fixed isolates the effect of gradient time.

The 10 min gradient is faster but has over-compressed the central cluster, especially peaks 6 and 7, so move slightly longer to recover resolution while staying in the no-time-penalty regime. A 12 min gradient should be a good local refinement between the well-resolved 20 min run and the overly steep 10 min run.

Resolution is improving as tG increases, with only the 6/7 pair still compressed, and there is still no time penalty at 12 min. Testing 14 min is the next logical local optimization to see whether that pair clears enough to raise the resolution term further while likely remaining within the zero-penalty time window.

The trend with gradient time is strongly favorable: the critical 6/7 pair keeps opening up and there is still no time penalty, so one more step longer is likely to further improve the resolution term. Testing 16 min checks whether we can approach full separation of the remaining close pair while staying efficient.

Since 15 min is unavailable and the optimum appears to lie between 14 and 16 min, adjust another lever that can slightly reduce retention without radically changing selectivity. Raising phi0 modestly should compress the gradient just enough to lower run time relative to the 14 min method while hopefully preserving near-complete resolution of the critical 6/7 pair.

Increasing phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved CRF by shortening the run while keeping the critical pair acceptably resolved, so one more small increase tests whether that trend continues. This is a focused local optimization around the current best settings with the same tG and temperature.

The best point so far is phi0 0.10, tG 14, but the limiting factor remains the 6/7 pair; a slightly longer gradient at the same improved starting strength may push that pair closer to full separation. This tests whether the gain in resolution can outweigh any small time penalty better than at phi0 0.05, tG 16.

We now know 16 min gives full resolution and phi0 0.10 improved the time term dramatically versus phi0 0.05, so test whether the slightly stronger start can reduce retention a bit further while still keeping the critical 6/7 pair above the full-resolution threshold. This is the most direct neighboring point to challenge the current best CRF.

You have already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000, so the safest choice is to remain in the same selectivity region and map robustness around the optimum rather than chase a higher score that is impossible. A slightly longer gradient should preserve full resolution and helps confirm the score plateau near the best method.

Since the maximum CRF has already been achieved at phi0 0.15, phi1 0.95, tG 16, the useful next step is robustness mapping with a small temperature change at the optimum composition program. Lowering T may slightly alter selectivity around the critical 6/7 pair while staying close to the known best region.

A 5 C decrease sharply worsened selectivity and shifted the critical overlap to peaks 5/6, so temperature is clearly influential near the optimum. Testing 45 C probes the opposite direction and may confirm whether 40 C is a local optimum or whether slightly higher temperature maintains the perfect score region.

Temperature deviations from 40 C strongly degrade selectivity, so keep T at the proven optimum and probe whether a slightly lower phi1 preserves full resolution while trimming the strongest-solvent portion of the gradient. This checks local robustness in endpoint composition around the already perfect method.

The optimum appears broad near phi0 0.10–0.15 at 16 min and 40 C, so the next useful boundary test is a further small increase in phi0. This checks whether retention can be shortened a bit more while still keeping the critical pair above the full-resolution threshold.

The perfect score at phi1 0.95 and the equally strong result at phi1 0.90 suggest endpoint composition is not critical in this region, so lowering phi1 further probes the robustness boundary while staying at the proven optimum phi0, tG, and temperature. This may preserve full resolution with no time penalty and define how broad the optimum is.

The data indicate the optimum is broad around phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.90–0.95 at 16 min and 40 C, with time penalty appearing when phi1 is lowered too far. Testing phi0 0.10 with phi1 0.90 explores the neighboring corner most likely to match the current best while confirming robustness of the perfect-score region.

With the optimum already found, the best use of remaining injections is to map robustness boundaries around it; 35 C and 45 C both degraded selectivity, so 50 C tests whether that trend continues at higher temperature. This adds information in an untested region without risking the discovered optimum itself.

The temperature series shows 40 C is best, with degradation at 35, 45, and 50 C, so 30 C completes the lower-side robustness map and confirms the shape of the temperature response. This explores an untested boundary while keeping the proven composition program fixed.

With the optimum already identified, a remaining useful untested corner is the combination of lower phi0 and slightly lower phi1 at the proven tG and temperature. This helps define the composition robustness surface around the best method and may reveal whether the perfect-score region extends toward weaker starting conditions.

The composition map suggests the optimum is near phi0 0.15 at 16 min and 40 C, with some loss already at phi0 0.20; testing phi0 0.25 defines that upper boundary more clearly. This is a final local robustness point in the most influential composition dimension around the best method.

Most nearby changes from the optimum have now been mapped; a remaining untested local boundary is a further reduction of phi1 at the best phi0, tG, and T. This will define whether endpoint strength continues to trade time for no selectivity benefit below phi1 0.85.

A remaining untested neighbor around the best region is the combination of phi0 0.10 with the longer 18 min gradient, which can show whether the low time penalty seen at phi0 0.10, tG 16 extends into a broader full-resolution plateau. This further maps the local response surface around the optimum without changing temperature.

A remaining untested local corner around the best region is the combination of slightly higher phi0 and slightly lower phi1, which helps complete the composition interaction map near the optimum. This can confirm whether the losses seen for phi0 0.20 and for lower phi1 are additive or if there is a compensating interaction.

The new second optimum at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.90, tG 16 suggests a nearby shorter gradient may still keep the critical pair above threshold while preserving a zero time penalty. Testing tG 14 is the most direct way to see whether this composition setting supports an equally efficient shorter run.

For the final injection, the most informative remaining local point is phi0 0.25 with phi1 0.90 at the proven 16 min and 40 C, to see whether lowering phi1 rescues the loss observed at phi0 0.25, phi1 0.95. This completes the composition map around the newly identified optimum at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.90.
